lesson_title: Converting Between Square Units of Area
hook_text: The radio said the fire burned 12 000 square metres. It was a thousand times bigger.
clip_script:
A community radio station in Mpumalanga reports on a veld fire near a farming town. The fire services say it burned 12 square kilometres of grassland. The news reader, converting for listeners, announces 12 000 square metres.

A Grade 8 learner frowns: that is barely two soccer pitches. A square kilometre is 1 000 metres by 1 000 metres — a million square metres. Twelve of them is 12 million. The reader used the length factor, 1 000, for an area. Area factors are squared: 100, 10 000, a million.
visual_style: A radio studio, then an aerial veld map; a tiny square labelled 12 000 square metres expands a thousandfold into a 4 by 3 kilometre rectangle of burned grass
call_to_action: Open the full session to convert any area without losing a factor.
